item.title: Norway and Finland leaders hold rare call with Putin
item.description:
Image source, AFP via Getty ImagesImage caption,
Norway and Finland say they are not acting on behalf of other European leadersByLaura Gozzi and Hafsa KhalilPublished27 October 2026, 13:12 GMTUpdated 1 hour ago
The leaders of Finland and Norway have held a joint call with Vladimir Putin - rare contact between the Russian president and European leaders.
Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said the aim of the call had been to "convey messages directly regarding future negotiations" towards peace. An end to the conflict in Ukraine "will not be achieved through silence," Stubb said.
Neither side suggested the needle had been moved on ending the war, which began when Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Although the Finnish leader said the conversation with Putin had been "frank and substantive," Støre added that there were "big differences in views" with Putin.
Several European leaders have recently shown willingness to engage with Russia directly, but both Stubb and Støre pointed out their initiative was taken in their capacity as neighbours of Russia, rather than on behalf of Europe as a whole.
"We've not set out to speak on behalf of anyone other than ourselves," Støre said.
Stubb added the call had been prepared in consultation with Ukraine and the US following a meeting between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, the Nordic leaders and US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo last week.
The first trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia talks since the start of the year are tentatively planned for early November in Abu Dhabi.
Zelensky later confirmed Stubb and Støre debriefed him after the call and said he was grateful for their "active support", while his Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the call had been "the right approach".

item.title: Truce begins in Ukraine city where residents ate weeds to survive
item.description:
Image source, Getty ImagesByDan Johnson, Reporting fromKyiv and Olga MalchevskaPublished27 October 2026, 02:58 GMTUpdated 4 hours ago
A truce has begun in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, where residents have been trapped without food, water and electricity.
Ukrainian officials and Russia's defence ministry say the limited ceasefire is being respected. The truce, which the White House said was secured by US First Lady Melania Trump, is meant to allow aid deliveries and a civilian evacuation on Friday.
Oleshky, along the front line in the Kherson region, is trapped on one side by the Dnipro River, which separates it from Ukrainian positions, and on the other by Russian forces.
Many residents have resorted to cooking garden weeds to survive, telling the BBC they are suffering extreme hunger and want to leave.
There are concerns that the truce will not hold, with one resident saying: "I don't believe in Russia's humanity."
Up to 6,000 people, including 200 children, remain in Oleshky and its surrounding areas, Kyiv believes, with only 1,700 still living in the city itself.
Before the war it was home to 24,000 people, but it was seized by Russia during the first days of its full-scale invasion in February 2022.
Conditions have become so desperate that not only is getting supplies into the city extremely difficult, but escape is highly dangerous because the routes out of Oleshky have been mined and subject to drone attack.
No shops are open, and the city has had no electricity, gas or water for three years.
Pope Leo XIV appealed earlier this month to Russia's President Vladimir Putin to allow food and medical aid into Oleshky as well as a safe evacuation, and urged his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky to co-operate with Moscow over a ceasefire.
The current truce is supposed to allow supplies in and enable roads to be cleared of mines to allow people safe passage out in an evacuation planned to take place on Friday....

item.title: Mbappé sorry for 'ill-judged' Mao remark after backlash in China
item.description:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption,
A backlash has erupted on Chinese social media over Mbappé's comments on a "Chinese dictator"ByKelly NgPublished27 October 2026, 07:15 GMTUpdated 6 hours ago
Kylian Mbappé has apologised for "ill-judged" comments he made about late Chinese leader Mao Zedong which led to him being dropped by several Chinese brands.
Mbappé had reportedly told French talk show The Bridge the meme "that makes me laugh the most, it's the one where there's a video of a guy, I think it's a Chinese dictator..." He then laughs as the clip cuts to a meme showing his face superimposed on an image resembling Mao.
The meme is part of a running joke about the Real Madrid forward being called a "dictator" because of his huge influence in football.
"My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world," Mbappé said in a statement.
"I apologise to everyone my words have upset."
Spain's La Liga also apologised, saying it "deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappé's recent comments have caused among Chinese fans".
The joke did not go down well in China, where Mao is revered by the Communist Party, despite his chaotic and often violent rule that left millions dead.
A few people came out in support of him on Chinese social media, but that is a rare response given China's tightly controlled internet, where people are expected to toe the party and government line on sensitive topics.
Few topics are as sensitive as Mao, which may explain why brands were so quick to terminate partnerships with a global sports star like Mbappé.
The original video is not available on the show's YouTube channel, and it's unclear when the interview hosted by Real Madrid's Aurélien Tchouaméni first aired. In clips that have been circulating online, Mbappé does not identify Mao by name. He says he "uses [the meme] with friends all the time".

item.title: Lula's comeback in Brazil dents Trump's ambitions for Latin America
item.description:
Image source, Getty ImagesByIone WellsPublished27 October 2026, 01:46 GMT
"Brazil will not accept being anyone's backyard," Brazil's left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva declared in his election victory speech, a message squarely aimed at Washington.
Domestic elections are rarely won on foreign policy, and this one was no different. But Lula's defiance against what he has described as US interference in Brazilian affairs evoked a patriotic spirit that proved an effective campaigning tool.
It also chimed with his wider brand of politics as a former union leader: standing up to powerful figures.
Paradoxically, it seems to have earned him President Donald Trump's respect. "I like Lula, we get along well," Trump said, responding to the result. "I didn't take sides," he added, before calling the election "terrible" and "rigged".

If that sounds muddled, it is because the relationship between the two men is not straightforward. Trump did not explicitly endorse Lula's rival Flávio Bolsonaro, who refused to recognise the result. But Trump was a close ally of Flávio's father, the former President Jair Bolsonaro.
When I spoke to Lula at his residence about a year ago, relations had hit rock bottom. He told me he had "no relationship" with Trump, that they had never spoken, and that he had no intention of picking up the phone. Trump had recently imposed punitive tariffs on Brazil, largely as a political response to Jair Bolsonaro's coup trial, which the US president called a "witch-hunt".
Rather than tiptoeing around Trump, as some US allies did, Lula fought back – and it paid off.

item.title: Dutch zookeeper dies after being mauled in leopard enclosure
item.description:
Image source, Getty ImagesByOlivia IrelandPublished15 minutes ago
An experienced keeper at a Dutch zoo has died days after being mauled in a leopard enclosure, the safari park has confirmed.
The woman, who had worked at Beekse Bergen park for 40 years, was caring for two Persian leopards in an indoor facility when she was attacked on Saturday.
She sustained injuries to her head and neck but despite undergoing surgery, the park confirmed her death on Tuesday.
An independent investigation will be launched into the incident, it added in a statement.
Announcing her death, Beekse Bergen - in the south of the Netherlands - said the keeper began her career there when she was 17 and had worked there on-and-off for four decades.
"Her passing has deeply affected us all, and our hearts go out to her family, friends, and loved ones. At this moment, our primary focus is on supporting her family and her colleagues," the statement added.
The two leopards, which are usually kept away from staff, had been brought inside due to bad weather conditions.
It is not clear exactly what happened in the enclosure because there are no CCTV cameras inside.
Local news website NL Times reported that despite her injures she managed to alert colleagues via her walkie-talkie. She was then taken to hospital in a helicopter in a critical condition before she died days later.
A park spokesperson told Omroep Brabant, a local media outlet, that the leopards were behaving naturally and they would not be euthanised.
"They are, and remain, predators."
Beekse Bergen said it would create a memorial location for guests and staff members to share their condolences.

item.title: Ghanaian twin brothers and US woman plead guilty to $9m romance scam
item.description:
Image source, TikTok/@arrangmentlancasterByGabriela Pomeroy and Thomas Naadi, BBC Africa, Reporting fromAccraPublished27 October 2026, 18:43 GMTUpdated 1 hour ago
Twin brothers from Ghana and an American woman have pleaded guilty to being part of an international criminal network that defrauded people on dating sites and social media.
The group targeted elderly people in the US and Europe, using fake identities to lure their victims into believing they were in a romantic relationship, before persuading them to transfer large sums of money into bank accounts in Ghana.
The 22-year-old twins, Jamal and Kamal Abubakari, and 53-year-old Amanda Joy Opoku-Boachie from Hawaii face up to 20 years in jail and will be sentenced next year.
Between July 2024 - April 2026, the victims collectively lost $9m (£6.7m).
While many of them were from Ohio - where the charges were brought - other victims were located in 24 other US states, as well as Germany and Austria.
As part of the plea, the Abubakaris and Opoku-Boachie agreed to forfeit pieces of jewellery which investigators seized during their arrest, including luxury watches, rings, chains and earrings.
Image source, US Attorney's Office, Northern District of OhioImage caption,
Jewellery was confiscated from the gang after they were arrested
The three accused go by several names:
Jamal Abubakari, also known as Jamal Abubakar and Arrangement
Kamal Abubakari, also known as Kamal Abubakar and Lancaster
Joy Opoku-Boachie, also known as Amanda Joy Glum and Amanda Joy Kessei Bierman
In recent months, US authorities have stepped up their crackdown on criminal networks operating in the US and West Africa which seek to defraud elderly Americans.
Earlier this month, FBI Director Kash Patel said it had made hundreds of arrests after dismantling a scam centre in Ghana.

item.title: Ballon d'Or ceremony raises case of French sports journalist jailed in Algeria
item.description:
Image source, AFP via Getty ImagesImage caption,
Christophe Gleizes, 37, is a French journalist who specialises in African football for the Paris-based So Foot magazineByBasma El AttiPublished27 October 2026, 13:59 GMTUpdated 5 hours ago
The plight of French sports journalist Christophe Gleizes, who is serving a seven-year prison sentence in Algeria, was highlighted at the Ballon d'Or ceremony.
Run by France Football magazine, the prestigious football awards were held in London where presenters Kate Scott and Thierry Henry dedicated the occasion to the 37-year-old reporter.
On a large screen behind them, it stated that he had been in jail for one year, three months and 27 days and alongside his photo was the hashtag "#FreeGleize".
He was arrested on a trip to Algeria where he had gone to report on a football club in Kabylie, a region where some people want self-determination. The authorities accused him of supporting terrorism.
"The Ballon d'Or France Football family would like to take this opportunity to dedicate this ceremony to Christophe Gleizes," said British broadcaster Scott and former Arsenal player and French striker Henry as the ceremony kicked off on Monday evening.
The event, held in London for the first time in its 70-year history, saw England and Bayern Munich strike Harry Kane crowned the world's top footballer of the year and London's City's Spanish midfielder Alexia Putellas taking the female prize.

item.title: Deaths in detention cells in Nigeria were entirely preventable, inquiry finds
item.description:
To play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser.
This video can not be playedFigure caption,
The BBC's Madina Maishanu shows the conditions inside the cell where so many diedByMadina Maishanu, BBC Africa, Reporting fromAbuja and Patrick JacksonPublished45 minutes ago
An inquiry into the deaths of 33 detainees in Nigeria's Minna state has found they died as a result of severe overcrowding, poor ventilation and failure by officers to respond to distress calls.
Forensic and medical evidence showed the "entirely preventable" deaths had resulted from acute respiratory failure linked to prolonged confinement, aggravated by heat stress and dehydration.
The evidence did not support initial claims of a disease outbreak.
The detainees were found dead on 17 September while being held by the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps on suspicion of illegal mining. The investigation found that the mining sites had been licensed.
'I have never felt heat like that' - a survivor on watching 33 cellmates die in Nigeria
Published22 September
Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo said those found responsible for the deaths would face the full force of the law.
He added that the detention hall had been cleaned before investigators arrived, raising concerns about possible attempts to compromise evidence.
Implicated officers will face suspension and the report would be forwarded to the attorney general of the federation for further legal action, Tunji-Ojo said.
Image source, EPAImage caption,
Family members reclaimed the bodies of their relatives from Minna's General Hospital last month
The investigating committee found that the raid on the miners had been conducted without an approved operational order, proper planning or consultation with the Mining Marshals Unit.

item.title: Controversial Islamic cleric shot dead in northern Nigeria
item.description:
Image source, Massussuka MediaImage caption,
Yahaya Masussuka was awarded a peace prize last year by Nigeria's Network for Good Governance and TransparencyByMansur AbubakarReporting fromAbujaPublished1 hour ago
A controversial Islamic cleric in Nigeria has been murdered outside his home in the northern state of Katsina.
Two assailants arrived on a motorcycle and shot Yahaya Masussuka in the town of Dutsin-Ma as he was saying goodbye to visitors on Monday evening, sources told the BBC.
The 47-year-old preacher and one of his guests, who was also shot, were rushed to hospital but both were pronounced dead by the attending doctor, police said.
It is not clear why Masussuka was targeted, but the cleric had received death threats on social media where he posted videos in which he rejected some elements of mainstream Islam, including what happens to people after their death.
It is widely believed in Islam that a person's soul will be questioned in the grave by two angels. If they answer correctly, their soul sleeps peacefully until the day of judgement - if not it will be tormented.
This understanding comes from what is known as the Hadith, a collection of texts believed to be the spoken words and actions of the Prophet Muhammad.
This serves as a key source of Islamic knowledge to help interpret the Quran, the central religious text of Islam.
But Masussuka based his teachings mainly on what was in Islam's holy book, questioned some of the hadiths - and did not believe that the dead were reawakened and questioned.
He was once jailed for nine months because he teased some respected scholars over their belief in this hadith and other teachings.
Masussuka, who had two wives and seven children, began preaching at the age of 13 in Quranic schools.
He later attended Al-Azhar University in Egypt and later went to Oman for further studies.

item.title: Jordan carries out deadly strike in Syria in retaliation for church attack
item.description:
Image source, Anadolu via Getty ImagesImage caption,
Syrian officials said five people were killed in the Jordanian strike on a village in the southern Daraa provinceByToby MannPublished27 October 2026, 02:40 GMT
Jordan has struck what its military says were "terrorist organisations" in Syria in retaliation for an attack on a Christian funeral last week that killed nine people.
Syrian health officials told state media that five people, including women, children and an elderly man, were killed in the strike on a village in the southern Daraa province. Jordan said its fighter jets had killed and wounded "several terrorists", without giving further details.
Jordan said it had co-ordinated with the Syrian government, but Syria said it had not been notified of Monday's attack.
It comes after nine people were killed and 34 injured in a shooting at a funeral in a Greek Orthodox church in Karak on Friday.
To play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser.

In response to the strike, Syria said it had closed a border crossing with Jordan.
"The decision includes the complete suspension of passenger and commercial traffic in both directions, to ensure the safety of travellers and workers at the crossing," Syrian authorities said in a statement carried by state media.
It added that it had "opened direct channels of communication" with Jordanian officials and had launched "comprehensive investigations to establish the full circumstances of the targeting".
Nassib is the only passenger and commercial border crossing between Jordan and Syria.
Earlier on Monday, senior government security officials said Jordanian security forces had arrested two brothers and their brother-in-law over the church attack.
The Public Security Directorate (PSD) said the unnamed "terrorists" were found hiding in an abandoned house in Karak before dawn.
